collector_scope.destination_scope: Global, including destinations outside the PhD-origin regions

usage_notes: This is a bounded source-research seed, not an exhaustive placement census or a denominator for ranking.
Records contain null for unknown years and unsupported fields. PhD graduation, job-market cycle, placement announcement year, and employment start are separate concepts.
The sources object resolves every source ID used in field_sources. Sources were reviewed on collected_at; access limitations are recorded.
Current employment is separated from the initial placement when initial title or first-job status is unverified.
A 2025–2026 roster is historical evidence only, not proof of being on the 2026–2027 market.
No ethnicity, nationality, citizenship or Chinese-background classification is collected or inferred.
Institution names alone are not used to infer undergraduate region. Unstated undergraduate region remains null.
Marketing is not automatically Quantitative Marketing; Economics is not automatically Industrial Organization.
Do not publish rates from this sample. Maintain cohort roster coverage and unknown outcomes before defining any denominator.
Reported source-table year is preserved separately when the table does not define whether it is graduation/cohort year or actual placement/start year.

maintenance_recommendations: Use stable person IDs and separate education, market-participation, employment-event and evidence tables. Retain historical evidence and corrections.
Define the primary population by doctoral-origin institution; record destinations globally so out-of-region jobs do not disappear from outcome denominators.
Store market cycle as a string and placement/announcement/start/graduation dates in distinct fields.
Allow Quantitative Marketing and IO labels simultaneously. Deduplicate by person for combined counts, and show label overlap.
Record postdocs and their later tenure-track outcomes as sequential events rather than overwriting the first destination.
Track each institution-cycle roster count, explicit outcome count, unknown outcome count and last verification date. Do not treat missing data as unemployment or zero placement.
Freeze annual snapshots, keep the current year marked provisional, and review historical postdoc transitions separately from first-placement totals.
